title: Slow English Podcast #187: Trinidad and Tobago

sentences.text: Today we will talk about Trinidad and Tobago.
It is a small, sunny and festive country in the Caribbean Sea.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Trinidad and Tobago?
Trinidad and Tobago is in the Caribbean near South America.
It is close to Venezuela.
The country has two main islands.
Trinidad, the larger island, Tobago, the smaller island.
It is surrounded by blue sea and has many beaches.
What is the capital city of Trinidad and Tobago?
The capital city is Port of Spain.
It is on the island of Trinidad.
It has offices, markets, museums, and colorful buildings.
It is also the home of Carnival, a big celebration.
Other towns include San Fernando, an important city in the South.
Scarborough, the main town on Tobago.
How many people live in Trinidad and Tobago?
About 1.5 million people live in the country.
Most people live on Trinidad and Tobago is less crowded.
The population is diverse with people of African, Indian, European, and mixed heritage.
What language do people speak in Trinidad and Tobago?
The official language is English.
But many people also speak Trinidadian Creole or Tobagonian Creole, local English dialects.
Some speak Hindi or Spanish in small communities.
The way of speaking is friendly, musical, and full of expressions.
What is the weather like in Trinidad and Tobago?
The country has a tropical climate.
It is hot and humid all year.
There is a rainy season from June to November.
The dry season is from December to May.
It is perfect for the beach, swimming, and sunshine.
What does Trinidad and Tobago look like?
The islands have white sand beaches and palm trees, hills, forests and rivers, coral reefs and clear blue sea, cities, villages, and fishing towns.
Tobago is more quiet and natural, great for relaxing.
What animals live in Trinidad and Tobago?
There are many animals such as monkeys, armadillos, and iguanas.
Colorful birds like hummingbirds and parrots, snakes, butterflies, and frogs.
In the sea, turtles, fish, and coral.
Many sea turtles come to lay eggs on the beaches.
What do people eat in Trinidad and Tobago?
Food is spicy, rich, and full of flavor.
People eat rice, peas, and roti flatbread.
Curry chicken, goat, or shrimp.
Doubles, fried bread with chickpeas and hot sauce.
Kalaloo, a green soup with coconut and vegetables.
Bacon shark, fried bread with fish.
There is also Chinese, Creole, and Indian influence in the food.
What do people drink in Trinidad and Tobago?
People drink water, coconut water, and fruit juice.
Mobby, a sweet drink made from tree bark.
Sodas and milk -based drinks.
Adults may enjoy rum, beer, or Caribbean cocktails.
Tropical fruits like mango, pineapple, and passion fruit are everywhere.
What is life like in Trinidad and Tobago?
Life is often easy -going, musical, and family -centered.
People enjoy spending time with friends and family, listening to music, especially Calypso and Soca, playing steelpan, the national instrument, going to the beach, dancing and celebrating.
Carnival, people are very friendly and love to talk and laugh.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Carnival, in February or March, with music, costumes, and dancing.
Independence Day, August 31st.
Diwali, Hindu Festival of Lights.
Eid al -Feder, celebrated by Muslims.
Christmas and New Year.
Each group celebrates its culture with respect and joy.
Some fun facts about Trinidad and Tobago.
It is the birthplace of steelpan music.
The country has more bird species than all of Europe.
The national instrument is the steel drum.
The flag is red, black, and white.
Tobago is known for coral reefs and diving.
Now you know many things about Trinidad and Tobago.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about the music, the beaches, and the celebrations.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
